rawAnswer: {"findings":[{"kind":"defect","severity":"medium","title":"Ignored-field branch changed from |= to &=, breaks private-member tracking","detail":"In GetObjectInfo the [IgnoreMember] field branch now does nonPublicMembersAreSerialized &= ... instead of |=. The flag starts false and fields are visited after properties, so &= can never set it. It can only clear it, and a public ignored field always does. Take a type where a non-public keyed property has set the flag. One public [IgnoreMember] field resets the flag to false. Deferred MemberNeedsKey diagnostics for non-public members are then never reported. MessagePackObjectAllowPrivateRequired at line 1352 can be skipped, and the PartialTypeRequired check at line 1382 is bypassed, so the generator may emit a formatter that cannot reach private members and does not compile. The property branch at line 899 still uses |=, so properties and fields now behave differently. A diagnostic created with a null location (Location.None) is therefore thrown away, even when it is about code in the current project. Roslyn allows analyzers to report Location.None; only a location in a syntax tree outside the compilation is rejected, so the remark in the code is wrong. Many diagnostics in TypeCollector can have a null location for types in the current project. One case: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null for a positional record property, whose syntax is a ParameterSyntax rather than a PropertyDeclarationSyntax. A [Key] with neither an int nor a string value on such a property used to throw. Now the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic silently disappears. UnionAttributeRequired, MessageFormatterMustBeMessagePackFormatter and PartialTypeRequired can be lost the same way when their syntax lookup returns null. This goes against N1 (no silent failures) and N2 (same-project behaviour unchanged).
